clause_or_section_seen: Annex III (1.2.1 per Art. 20(9); retention sub point unverified)
requirement_paraphrase: Law firm summary: safety functions must not be changed by ML beyond limits set in the risk analysis; self-learning machines must not act outside defined task and movement space; safety-decision data kept at least one year; technical file must describe limits, data, development and validation of autonomous machines. Note: the one year retention of safety decision data is not found in Arts 10, 11 or 13 and is not verified in Annex III; an unofficial reproduction places it in 1.2.1 second list point (b). The 10 year technical documentation retention in Art. 10(3) is a different rule.

instrument: NHTSA Standing General Order 2021-01 (Third Amended) crash reporting
requirement_paraphrase: Named manufacturers/operators must report ADS and L2 ADAS crashes: most severe within 5 days, others monthly; ADS thresholds stricter than ADAS; crash within 30 seconds of system use.
applies_to: Named entities in US (ADS L3-5 and L2 ADAS)

edition_or_version: Formal 2.3 (adopted Oct 2023 per OMG page); 2.4 beta listed
status_note: OMG spec page lists 2.4 as beta (informational); formal version is the one to follow for compliance
requirement_paraphrase: Defines a metamodel/UML profile for representing assurance cases (auditable claims, arguments, evidence) and a graphical notation for tool exchange.
applies_to: Tool vendors and developers exchanging assurance cases

requirement_paraphrase: Blog lists topics the standard covers: dependability, V&V, tool qualification, COTS and legacy components, lifecycle, maintenance, metrics/SPIs, conformance and independent assessment; three-step claim/argument/evidence structure.

instrument: RICS article: GNSS spoofing and mitigation in the Arabian Gulf
status_note: Professional-body practice note; not a standard
requirement_paraphrase: Recommends machine-control and robotic users configure alarms for coordinate jumps, fuse GNSS with IMU/LiDAR, use authenticated corrections, keep RTK fallback and validate time sync; surveyors to use multi-session observations and cross-checks.
applies_to: Surveyors, machine-control, construction in the Gulf

instrument: UK CAA guidance on GNSS jamming (via SUAS News report)
status_note: Secondary press report of CAA guidance
requirement_paraphrase: Reports that CAA advises operators not to rely solely on satellite navigation during known jamming trials (be ready for alternatives such as dead reckoning), notes jamming can disable drone return-to-home and digital geofencing, and urges pilots to report jamming not announced in advance.

status_note: Superseded by standard per other row; status of OOI not checked
requirement_paraphrase: 2020 article says UL 3300 evaluation covers multidirectional mobility, fire and shock hazards, external manipulation, user classes and use surroundings, in settings with people present.

UL states the safety case must show that relevant objects are detected and classified within the intended ODD, and must show a robust mix of analysis, simulation, closed-course and safe public-road testing for the initial vehicle and each software update; no fixed road-mile number is required.
Edition 3 added requirements on post-incident behaviour; also added a more precise definition of one preferred safety performance indicator (SPI) form.

edition_or_version: UL 3115 OOI published 31 Oct (year not on page; release dated Nov 2025); edition not stated
status_note: Outline of Investigation, not a full UL Standard; paired with UL 3300 for robots in UL certification service
requirement_paraphrase: UL says UL 3115 assesses AI-based products on robustness, reliability, transparency, accountability, privacy, fairness, safety, security and freedom from bias; UL service page says it is meant to be used with a product standard such as UL 3300 for SCIEE robots.
applies_to: AI-based products; consumer and commercial robots in homes and public spaces

edition_or_version: Guidance v1.1 (file SACE_v1_1.pdf); fetch tool reported 'July 2026'
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage system-level process: operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation (ODM boundary and minimum risk strategy), verification; each with a GSN pattern; ML components handled via AMLAS.
applies_to: Autonomous systems in complex environments (incl. robots, drones)

instrument: SACE Safety Assurance of autonomous systems in Complex Environments
clause_or_section_seen: Eight stages; Stage 1 Activity 2 (Operational Domain Model)
requirement_paraphrase: Eight-stage process (operating context, hazardous scenarios, safe operating concept, safety requirements, design, hazardous failures, out-of-context operation, verification), each ending in a GSN pattern; the Operational Domain Model defines where safety is argued.
applies_to: Autonomous systems operating in complex environments

instrument: SACE Safety Assurance of autonomous systems in Complex Environments
requirement_paraphrase: SACE covers only the development phase before deployment; operational safety management is out of scope. Simulation is described as helping reviewers understand scenarios (Activity 3), as additional analysis to corroborate hazard validation (Activity 8), and as one option for validating the safe operating concept, including hardware-in-the-loop (Note 13); the guidance says justifying simulation representativeness is challenging.

instrument: UAE information paper to MIDANPIRG/20 & RASG-MID/10 (ICAO site)
status_note: Add: GCAA site now also lists CAR-UA-ATO Issue 01 and CAR-UAM Issue 1 (titles seen); planned CAR-Airspace Part U-space reported adopted in Mar 2025 (see C60)
requirement_paraphrase: States current UAE rules generally limit unmanned aircraft to daylight, VLOS and below 400 ft AGL, with other operations (night, BVLOS, above 400 ft, multiple UA) needing special approvals; hobbyist flights were largely kept out of controlled airspace while commercial operations have since been allowed to expand into it under approval; lists CAR-UAC, UAD, UAEV, UAX (experimental) and UAR under Federal Decree-Law 26/2022, and planned CAR-Airspace, CAR-UTMSP, CAR-UTM and CAR-USP/ASP. GNSS and remote ID not discussed.
